Wesley Sneijder on Japan's dominant 4-0 victory over Tunisia at the World Cup:

🗣️ “People might look at the Netherlands drawing 2-2 with Japan earlier in the tournament and only focus on the result. But after watching them destroy Tunisia 4-0, I can tell you that draw looks more impressive with every passing day.”

“When we faced Japan, you could immediately feel how organized they were. They never stopped running, never stopped pressing, and never gave you a second to relax on the ball.”

“A lot of teams have talented players, but Japan have something even more dangerous right now complete belief. Every player understands his role and every player is willing to sacrifice for the team.”

“This 4-0 victory wasn't just a win. It was a statement to the rest of the World Cup. Tunisia simply could not live with the speed, movement, and intensity that Japan brought to the match.”

“What impressed me most is that Japan don't play like outsiders anymore. They play like a team that genuinely believes it belongs among the best nations in the tournament.”

“When the Netherlands played them, there were moments where they caused us serious problems. They were fearless. They attacked with confidence and defended with incredible discipline.”

“That's why I'm not surprised by what happened against Tunisia. The signs were already there. Japan have been building towards a performance like this.”

“If they continue playing with this level of confidence and organization, they will become one of the most dangerous teams in the knockout rounds. Nobody will be excited to face them.”

“Before the tournament started, people talked about Japan as a dark horse. After performances like this, they're forcing people to have a completely different conversation.”

“And trust me, after seeing them up close and watching them dismantle Tunisia 4-0, I can say with confidence that Japan are becoming one of the teams capable of shocking the entire football world.”
xThreads.translatedText:
ワールドカップでのチュニジア戦、日本代表の圧倒的な4-0勝利について、ウェズレイ・スナイデルが語る：

🗣️ 「大会序盤にオランダが日本と2-2で引き分けた時、人々は結果だけを見たかもしれない。しかし、彼らがチュニジアを4-0で粉砕するのを見て、あの引き分けは日が経つごとにますます印象的になっていると言える。」

「日本と対戦した時、彼らがどれほど組織的であるかをすぐに感じた。彼らは走るのを止めず、プレスを止めず、ボールを持っている間に一瞬たりとも休ませてくれなかった。」

「多くのチームには才能ある選手がいるが、今の日本にはさらに危険なもの、つまり完全な自信がある。すべての選手が自分の役割を理解し、チームのために犠牲を払うことを厭わない。」

「この4-0の勝利は単なる勝利ではなかった。ワールドカップの他のチームへの声明だった。チュニジアは、日本が試合にもたらしたスピード、動き、強度に全く対応できなかった。」

「私が最も感銘を受けたのは、日本がもはやアウトサイダーのようにプレーしていないことだ。彼らは、大会で最高の国々の中に自分たちが属していると心から信じているチームのようにプレーしている。」

「オランダが彼らと対戦した時、彼らは我々に深刻な問題を引き起こす瞬間があった。彼らは恐れを知らなかった。自信を持って攻撃し、信じられないほどの規律で守備をした。」

「だから、チュニジア戦での出来事にも驚かない。その兆候はすでにあった。日本はこのようなパフォーマンスに向けて着実に力をつけてきたのだ。」

「もし彼らがこの自信と組織力を保ってプレーし続ければ、ノックアウトステージで最も危険なチームの一つになるだろう。誰も彼らと対戦したがらないだろう。」

「大会が始まる前、人々は日本をダークホースと呼んでいた。このようなパフォーマンスの後では、彼らは人々に全く異なる議論を強いている。」

「そして信じてほしい、彼らを間近で見て、チュニジアを4-0で解体するのを見た後、日本はフットボール界全体を驚かせることができるチームの一つになりつつあると自信を持って言える。」

Sir Alex Ferguson on Japan's dominant 4-0 victory over Tunisia at the World Cup:

🗣️ “I've watched football for decades, and one thing I've learned is that truly dangerous teams are often the ones people underestimate. Japan are no longer a team that should be underestimated by anybody.”

“A 4-0 victory at a World Cup doesn't happen because of luck. It happens because of preparation, discipline, quality, and a group of players completely committed to a common goal.”

“What stands out to me is their mentality. They don't play with fear. They don't play with doubt. They play with the confidence of a team that genuinely believes it belongs among the very best nations in football.”

“Before the tournament, the conversation was always about the traditional giants. But while everyone was busy discussing the usual favourites, Japan were quietly building something very special.”

“The best teams are not always the ones with the biggest names. The best teams are the ones that function as a unit, trust each other completely, and fight for every single moment. Japan have all of those qualities.”

“What should worry the rest of the world is that they are getting stronger with every match. That's usually the sign of a team capable of going very deep into a tournament.”

“When I watch Japan, I see hunger. I see organization. I see players willing to run, sacrifice, and work for each other. Those are the foundations of championship-winning teams.”

“People might still hesitate to call them favourites, but if they continue producing performances like this, that debate won't last much longer.”

“Every major tournament has a team that captures momentum and belief. Right now, Japan are building both at an alarming rate.”

“And trust me, if I were managing one of the traditional powerhouses in this World Cup, Japan would be one of the last teams I'd want to face. Because they look like a team that believes its destiny is much bigger than simply participating.”

🚨Jürgen Klopp on Japan’s dominant 4–0 victory over Tunisia at the World Cup:

🗣️ “Right now, we need to start asking ourselves the real question: are Japan really underdogs anymore?

“After what they’ve shown in their first two matches, I don’t think so. They’ve been a handful for every opponent they’ve faced.

“People need to stop looking down on Japan. I’ve had the opportunity to work with Japanese players, and I can tell you they bring incredible discipline, intensity, and professionalism.

“In my opinion, they pose a bigger threat at this World Cup than many of the traditional favourites. Teams like Argentina, Portugal, France, and others will know they are in for a very difficult game if they face Japan.

“This tournament should be a reminder that football is not about reputation—it’s about performances. And right now, Japan are performing at an exceptionally high level.

“A 4–0 win at the World Cup doesn’t happen by accident. It happens because you have a clear identity, a strong structure, and players who fully believe in what they are doing.

“What I love most about this Japan team is their intensity. They play with courage, they press together, they defend together, and they attack with real purpose.

“The scary thing is they never stop. At 3–0, at 4–0, they keep running, keep pressing, and keep looking for more. That is the mentality of a team that believes it can achieve something special.

“This World Cup should finally show everyone that Japan deserve far more respect on the football map.

“Any team drawn against Japan in the next round will not be happy. They will be asking themselves one question: how do we stop them?”
